To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in hypertrophic human atria a shift in myosin heavy-chain isoenzymes occurs and in hypertrophic ventricles the ventricular myosins become enriched in light chain-1 of the atrial type.

in pressure-overloaded hypertrophied ventricles the myosin light-chain-1 is shifted from the predominant light-chain-1 towards the atrial light-chain-1 and that the myosin-heavy-chain peptide patterns of hypertrophied atrial tissues are different from those of the normal atria.

1) the myosin light-chain complement in hypertrophied human atria comprises a new component (ALC- 1); 2) ALC-1 also appears in ventricular tissue of hypertrophic hearts; 3) the peptide patterns of the myosin subunits in normal and hypertrophed ventricle do not differ, whereas the peptide patterns of atrial myosins from hypertrophed atrium do.

in hypertrophied hearts the myosin light-chain complement is altered in a way that ventricular light chains appear in the hypertrophied atrial tissues, and that atrial myosins appear in the hypertrophic ventricular tissues.

in hypertrophied human ventricles a shift towards the atrial type of myosins is taking place, which is most pronounced in pressure-overloaded hearts, and that the myosin light-chain complement is also altered, which is most obvious in pressure-overloaded right ventricles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the myosin isoenymes in human hypertrophied hearts are characterized by a shift from the normal ventricular myosins to atrial myosins in the atria and from ventricular to atrial myo-sins in the ventricles.
in hypertrophied hearts the myosin light and heavy chains are not only modified in a quantitative manner but also qualitatively.

hypertrophy in the human ventricle is associated with a shift in the myosin light-chain composition, and that hypertrophy in human atria is characterized by the expression of a myosin heavy chain different from the one in normal atria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in hypertrophied human atria the ventricular light chain-1 is replaced by the atrial light-chain-1.

the myosin light-chain complement in hypertrophied human ventricles is not as homogeneous as previously assumed and that the myosins of atria and ventricles are more closely related to each other than to their own myosins in the normal heart.
pressure-overload hypertrophy is associated with a shift in the myosin light-chain complement and with a change in the myosinal heavy-chain type.
